purpose: Streaming response fixtures for Gemini Interactions (line contract sections on streaming, errors and cases GI-06 to GI-08). Each client's production parser replays every case and the body, thinking, citations, web-search evidence, error and terminal state land in their respective fields. Taken from official documentation samples; real recorded samples are added under recorded_samples and do not replace this group. Unrelated to the sibling expected.json (the leg-1 tool call corpus) and must not be merged into it: that list's entry count is locked by tests on all clients and on desktop.

provenance_legend.official: frames are byte-for-byte from the official documentation samples
provenance_legend.official_adapted: taken from an official sample with only the noted fields changed
provenance_legend.schema: the official docs have no streaming sample, so it is synthesized from the OpenAPI schema

conventions.wire: Each frame is `event: <event_type>` + `data: <json>` + a blank line, LF line endings; a normal end is interaction.completed followed by `event: done` / `data: [DONE]`. The parser relies on the event_type inside data, and `[DONE]` is not parsed as JSON.
conventions.step_delta: In step.delta, index and delta sit at the top level of the frame with no step object; step.start's step.type is used only for grouping and is not a filter for body text.
conventions.ignored_delta_types: thought_signature and google_search_call deltas do not enter the body, thinking or evidence; an unknown delta.type / event_type is ignored with one local diagnostic and does not interrupt the stream.
conventions.search_evidence: A google_search_result delta whose is_error is not true counts as one web-search evidence item; the official streaming sample carries no result (the schema marks it required), so the parser must not require result to be present.
conventions.citations: For entries with type=url_citation in text_annotation_delta.annotations[], start_index / end_index are passed through unchanged (clients do not slice by them). The unit is UTF-8 bytes: the real sample gemini_interactions_live_search.sse (Chinese body of 198 characters / 558 bytes; citation 125..275 overflows when sliced by character and yields a complete clause when sliced by byte) agrees with the schema, so the official guide's by-character example code is wrong for non-ASCII bodies.
conventions.text: expected.text is the original concatenation of all text deltas in arrival order (not trimmed); thinking likewise concatenates thought_summary.content.text.
conventions.terminal: completed = an interaction.completed with status=completed was received; incomplete = status=incomplete (content already emitted is kept and the reply ends as truncated output, same as max_tokens); error = an error frame was received, or interaction.completed has status=failed (code recorded as interaction_failed) or requires_action (this line sends no client tools; recorded as interaction_requires_action); interrupted = status=cancelled, or the connection closed with neither completed nor error. Error phase: before_content = no body or thinking so far (handled as an upstream error); after_content = content already exists (the message fails, the received content is kept, and nothing is resent). error.code is a string (official schema: a URI-style identifier), not the integer code of generateContent.
conventions.citations_dedupe: When a client compares citations, both sides are first de-duplicated by url (keeping the first occurrence and its range) and then compared: all three clients merge sources by url in production (iOS CitationAccumulator.ingest, Web mergeUrlCitations, Android ChatRepository to CitationParser.mergeCitations), so users see a list of distinct sources and clients do not slice by index; dropping later ranges of the same url has no visible effect. A parser that outputs every entry unchanged (Android) also satisfies this after de-duplication. The reference parser's expected keeps every entry unchanged.
